proof:
# Residual-projection exit martingales and unbounded critical overshoot
distance-to-exit factors. It then shows that those factors are not bounded
by cap mass, fiber volumes, or the original hitting weights alone, even
for an attained globally critical cap in an actual convex family. The
example is above the OC target. No below-target impossibility is claimed.

## 1. A single barycentric row with empty destinations

Work with positive full-dimensional d-dimensional fibers of an actual
convex body, d>=1. Fix a nonvertical cap H={ell(z,x)>=0}, so its continuous
normal is nonzero. Define its residual root at a measured base by

    f(z)=|C_z intersect {ell(z,x)<0}|^(1/d).

Suppose p=sum_j theta_j z_j, with theta_j>0 and sum theta_j=1, and f(p)>0.
All original source and destination fibers have positive d-volume. For a
destination with f(z_j)>0 set t_j=1 and b_j=z_j. For a destination with
f(z_j)=0, let t_j be the first exit fraction from the positive residual
projection along the segment from p to z_j, and put

    b_j=p+t_j(z_j-p).

Then 0<t_j<=1, the residual root at b_j is zero, and the closed residual
section C_(b_j) intersect {ell<=0} is nonempty. The difference between
strict and closed residuals has d-volume zero, because the continuous
normal is nonzero.

Here are the endpoint details. Along the segment all original sections
have positive d-volume by Minkowski inclusion. At an interior parameter,
their compact sections are Hausdorff continuous: an interior section
point can be approximated from either side by combining it with a fixed
positive section farther along that side, while compactness gives upper
continuity. A nonempty strict residual in a full-dimensional section has
positive volume, by mixing its point with an interior section point.
The minimum cap margin is therefore negative before the first exit and
zero there. At t_j<1, continuity proves nonempty closed contact and zero
residual volume. If t_j=1, upper semicontinuity gives a limiting contact
point; a strictly negative margin at the destination would make its
residual positive, contradicting its definition. Nonverticality gives
the zero d-volume of this contact section. Positivity at p and local
continuity give t_j>0.

Set

    c=sum_j theta_j/t_j
      =1+sum_(f(z_j)=0) theta_j(1/t_j-1),
    hat_theta_j=(theta_j/t_j)/c.                        (1)

These are positive weights summing to one, and

    sum_j hat_theta_j b_j=p,                           (2)

since the numerator of the displacement from p is
sum_j theta_j(z_j-p)=0. Thus the truncated row becomes a martingale row
only AFTER this reweighting. Keeping the old weights after shortening
the exiting segments generally destroys the barycenter.

The closed residual sections at the b_j are nonempty convex sets.
Their weighted Minkowski combination is contained in the source's
closed residual section. Brunn--Minkowski, allowing lower-dimensional
nonempty boundary sections, gives

    sum_(f(z_j)>0) theta_j f(z_j) <= c f(p).             (3)

Equation (3) is a precise extension through fully captured destinations.
Their contribution is not silently set to zero in an unchanged Jensen
inequality. The exact additional term is

    f(p) sum_(f(z_j)=0) theta_j(1/t_j-1).               (4)

Every exiting original destination is fully captured by H and can be
charged by its actual fiber volume, but (4) also contains its geometric
overshoot factor 1/t_j-1.

## 2. A finite stopped-flow construction

Use the audited KKT absorbing-chain notation: T is the finite transition
matrix, D is the diagonal stopping matrix, T1+D1=1, each full row has
base barycenter equal to its source, and every D_ii>0 on the retained
positive-height states. Fix H as above. Let I be the subset of states
with positive residual root f_i. For i in I and j outside I with
T_ij>0, construct the first-exit fraction t_ij from Section1. Put

    c_i=1+sum_(j outside I) T_ij(1/t_ij-1).             (5)

Replace the original process, while at i in I, by the following choices:

* continue to j in I with probability T_ij/c_i;
* stop at the original state i with probability D_ii/c_i;
* stop at the boundary point b_ij with probability T_ij/(c_i t_ij)
  for each j outside I.

These probabilities sum to one and their physical base barycenter is
p_i. Each boundary stop retains its original fully captured label j,
although its new base b_ij need not be integer. The construction is used
only to prove a volume inequality; it does not propose a new center in S.

The residual root is a nonnegative supermartingale for this modified
process by Section1. All state values are bounded. There are finitely
many positive c_i, and the stopping probability at an original state is
at least min_i D_ii/c_i>0. Thus the probability of continuing for m steps
tends to zero geometrically, justifying the terminal inequality directly
by iterated finite conditioning and bounded convergence.

For an explicit matrix formula, write C=diag(c_i), restrict T and D to I,
and set

    R=C^(-1) T_(I,I),
    W=(I-R)^(-1) C^(-1) D_(I,I).                       (6)

The inverse is the convergent nonnegative series sum_(m>=0)R^m. Then
W_ij is the probability of finally stopping at the original state j
when starting at i; its missing row mass is the probability of a new
boundary stop. Since those boundary residual roots vanish,

    sum_j W_ij f_j <= f_i.                             (7)

This is an exact finite optional-stopping statement. The weights W are
not the original KKT terminal weights. Replacing W by the original
coupling would require a new comparison that controls the factors c_i.

## 3. A globally critical family with fixed budget and unbounded factors

Use the proved exact-depth theorem
`candidate 1d1be0b22c707856`. Fix d>=2 and
a d-simplex T of volume one, with barycentric coordinates lambda_i and
centroid g. Choose one vertex as the origin and let A=epsilon T be a
homothetic copy about that vertex. Choose lambda_1 as the barycentric
coordinate of a different vertex, so lambda_1(0)=0. Choose

    0<epsilon^d<=rho_d,

where rho_d>0 is the explicit proved scalar threshold in the cited
theorem. Put the actual fibers A,T,T at integer bases -1,0,1 and take
their convex hull C. Their exact global maximum raw mixed depth is

    Q=gamma_d+epsilon^d,

uniquely at (0,g). This dependency controls every ambient oblique
halfspace, not merely the caps displayed below.

For every L>=2, the cap

    H_L={lambda_1(x)-Lz>=1/(d+1)}                      (8)

has exact mass Q. It fully captures A, cuts the middle T by its canonical
centroid cap of mass gamma_d, and excludes the +1 copy of T. Thus it is
an actual globally critical cap through (0,g) for every such L.

For clarity, form a finite complete cap cover by all canonical caps

    P_i(L)={lambda_i(x)-Lz>=1/(d+1)},
    Q_i(L)={lambda_i(x)+L(z-1)>=1/(d+1)},
                 0<=i<=d.                             (9)

The P_i have mass Q, and the Q_i have mass gamma_d. Their one-cap
residual minima at the three bases are

    (e_-1,e_0,e_1)=(0,c,c),
    c=(1-gamma_d)^(1/d).                              (10)

The unique convex threshold optimum is h_-1=h_0=h_1=c. Indeed h_0>=c
and convexity gives h_-1+h_1>=2h_0, whence the sum of dth powers is at
least 3c^d, attained only by these equal heights. The constraint h_1>=c
is also satisfied.

Writing s=d c^(d-1), take mu_(0,-1)=mu_(0,1)=s,
lambda_0=3s and all other lambda entries zero. These are exact KKT
multipliers. The normalized terminal row from 0 assigns weight 1/3
to each of -1,0,1. At H_L the residual roots are

    0, c, 1.

Along the segment to the fully captured destination -1, write z=-t.
The actual section is

    C_-t=[1-(1-epsilon)t] T,       0<=t<=1.

This follows from A subset T: mixing the -1 and 0 fibers gives this
section, and using any additional +1 weight only increases the A
coefficient and makes the homothetic section smaller. The minimum of
lambda_1 on every such section is zero. Its strict residual under (8)
is nonempty exactly when

    1/(d+1)-Lt>0.

Consequently its exact first-exit fraction is

    t_(0,-1)=1/[(d+1)L].                              (11)

Applied to the normalized terminal row, (1) therefore gives

    c_row=1+[(d+1)L-1]/3 -> infinity.                  (12)

The same factor appears for the KKT one-step process, whose middle row
has transition probabilities 1/3 to each endpoint and stopping
probability 1/3 at the middle. All original fiber volumes, original
hitting weights, source root c, and the actual critical budget Q remain
unchanged while L increases. The fully captured fiber volume is always
epsilon^d.

Thus no bound on these necessary reweighting/overshoot factors can depend
only on that fixed volume, mass, and probability data. Global criticality
alone does not supply such a bound for every critical cap. One could
still try to optimize the choice of critical cap, or use the below-OC
hypothesis in an essential additional argument; neither is established
by this example.

The example is OC-safe: the cited theorem explicitly gives normalized
depth (gamma_d+epsilon^d)/(2+epsilon^d)>gamma_d/2. Its purpose is to
identify the exact missing geometric control in an unconditional
first-exit charge, not to contradict the target theorem.
